steps.note: Raw goat's milk is set mainly by its own mesophilic lactic flora, with at most 5 ml of rennet per 100 l.
The curd is ladled by hand into perforated moulds in several goes.
It drains by itself, with no pressure, for at least 18 hours from the start of moulding.
The cheeses are turned out and salted over all their faces, and eaten fresh instead of being ripened.

links.name: Sainte-Maure de Touraine PDO, product specification (French Ministry of Agriculture)

sources.text: The lactic set (18-48 h at up to 25 °C, a trace of rennet), hand ladling, slow draining and surface salting are from the specification of one lactic goat cheese; the cheese itself is then ashed and ripened at least 10 days, which this fresh version leaves out.
